title: Estimation
summary: Round each number to 1 significant figure, then calculate: whole numbers, then fractions, then decimals. Built for about two lessons, worked through in order.

els.text: Estimate the answer to a calculation by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.

•  Round a number to 1 significant figure
•  Calculate with the rounded numbers
•  Say whether an estimate is sensible
Name the first significant figure of each number.

slides.title: Round to 1 s.f.

items.title: Round $48$ to 1 significant figure
question: Round $48$ to 1 significant figure.
explanation: The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit, so the rounding digit is $4$ and the decider, the digit after it, is $8$.
The decider is $8$, which is $5$ or more, so round up: $8 \ge 5$
Add 1 to the rounding digit and drop (or zero) everything after it: $50$

items.title: Round $84$ to 1 significant figure

explanation: The first significant figure is the first non-zero digit, so the rounding digit is $8$ and the decider, the digit after it, is $4$.
The decider is $4$, which is less than $5$, so round down: $4 \lt 5$
Keep the rounding digit and drop (or zero) everything after it: $80$

slides.brief: Build from the digit rule to the edges in one set. Seven fixed whole numbers: two-digit, three- and four-digit, then three edge cases (rounding up to the next place, exactly halfway, a zero in the middle).

els.text: An approximate answer, found by rounding the numbers first.
A digit that carries value. The first significant figure is the first digit that is not zero.
Close to, but not exactly equal to. The symbol is $\approx$.
To estimate is to find an approximate answer by rounding each number to 1 significant figure before calculating.
Set out the working, then check on a calculator.

items.title: The calculator slip
question: Kofi types $36 \times 58$ into his calculator and gets $208$.
Use an estimate to show that this cannot be right.
answer: Round each number to 1 significant figure: $36 \to 40$ and $58 \to 60$.
explanation: $208$ is far too small. Kofi has missed a digit: the exact answer is $2088$.

Four fraction bars (a sum, a difference, a product, and one with a sum on the bottom), then four with a term: a fraction plus a whole number, a whole number minus a fraction, or a fraction times a whole number (round the numbers, work out the fraction, then add, subtract or multiply).

els.text: Is $0.39$ nearer to $0$ or to $1$? Would $0$ be a useful estimate? What is the first significant figure of $0.39$?
The first significant figure is the first digit that is not zero: the $3$. Round to that place and $0.39$ becomes $0.4$.
Zeros before the first digit only hold the place.

els.text: What happens when we divide by a number less than 1?

els.text: Which is bigger: $6 \div 2$ or $6 \div 0.5$? Predict first, then check.
Dividing by a number less than $1$ makes the answer bigger. $6 \div 0.5$ asks how many halves are in $6$.

els.text:
•  Round every number to 1 significant figure first.
•  Then calculate with the rounded numbers.
•  A fraction bar means divide: round the top and the bottom first.
•  Check the size of your answer: does it make sense?
